recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No further FHIR core work is needed for FHIR-17438 unless a future publisher regression hides canonical target types again; do not duplicate the already-published FHIR-17433 and FHIR-17537 reconciliations.
issue_request: FHIR-17438 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked for canonical elements such as QuestionnaireResponse.questionnaire to show allowed resource types on the main resource page, and for canonical documentation to clarify that allowed target lists are constrained to resource types with canonical url elements.
initial_application: The Jira application comment points to GH#9c858ce3d2, represented by git commit 9c858ce3d24372d302e90f0440fa167b199ed845. That commit linked the canonical datatype description to references.html#canonical-list and added the canonical-list anchor to source/references.html. Later editorial changes preserved that guidance; the face-up display behavior is verified in current publisher output rather than by a separate Jira-tagged source hunk.
additional_context: The Zulip topic cited by the issue records the canonical targetProfile discussion and FHIR-17438 being logged because canonical allowed types were not visible enough. FHIR-17433 covers the related ElementDefinition.targetProfile rule for canonical and is already audited on the combined branch. FHIR-17537 covers canonical(Any) target-list guidance and is already represented on the combined branch with a source fix. Confluence searches found no FHIR-17438 references.
reconciliation: No source change was made. QuestionnaireResponse remains an active resource in source/fhir.ini, QuestionnaireResponse.questionnaire is type canonical with targetProfile Questionnaire, source/datatypes.html links canonical to resources with a url property, and source/references.html retains the canonical resource list and canonical(Any) restriction. The current CI build renders QuestionnaireResponse.questionnaire as canonical(Questionnaire) on the main page and in syntax examples.
